analysis:
The change is docs-only (docs/reference/configuration.md): the last-updated date moves from 2026-10-30 to 2026-10-31, and the head changes the "Cluster runtime facts" section (head ~lines 923-1015). The supplied units are the BASE text, lines 1-313 and 314-484. The changed ranges at base 923+ fall beyond the supplied base text, and the patch excerpt is truncated. Only the first part of the new text is visible: signed releases register `cluster_runtime` in the `POST /v1/releases` payload, and a coordinator that accepts the block derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. I could not verify the rest of the head changes.

No executable code changed, so there is no direct regression in the provider, in App Attest, or in the prefix cache (T-041). The visible base lines contain no secrets and no new attack surface.

The truncated patch describes a possible trust-model change: release-registered cluster runtime facts auto-derive approvals and pair-serving grants, where before an operator approval file was the source. That touches A-005/A-011/A-017 (release API key, binary hash registry, build qualifications). It is backend-owned and outside this repo's scope. Reviewers of the remaining units should check whether the new documentation claims approval derivation without independent operator qualification, and whether pair-serving grants stay bound to a verified build identity and to revocation.

The base-side configuration documentation is unchanged and matches the existing threat model (T-041 default-on encrypted SSD prefix cache, TB-011 worker opt-in, TB-012 add-on hold, TB-013 sandbox). I flagged no uncertainty beyond the truncated patch.
